result.title: Page 1
result.summary: The Shrewsbury Contributory Retirement Board seeks written proposals from qualified investment consultants for its Massachusetts public pension system, governed by Chapter 32, applicable state laws and regulations, and relevant federal investment-adviser rules. The system has approximately $125 million in assets, an 86.6% funding ratio, and active, inactive, and retired members. The consultant will advise the Board on investment policy, asset allocation, portfolio and manager selection, and investment performance; monitor investments and managers; prepare reports; attend meetings; and coordinate with Board staff. Proposers must demonstrate qualifications, regulatory compliance, and relevant experience, and provide required proposal and fee information. The anticipated contract is for five years, with a possible renewal or extension. The Board retains discretion to select a consultant, reject any or all proposals, cancel the procurement, or terminate the contract, including with notice as specified.

result.title: Page 2
result.summary: The Shrewsbury Retirement Board invites proposals for investment consulting services. Proposals were due by 12:00 p.m. on Friday, May 11, 2018, at 100 Maple Avenue, Shrewsbury, MA 01545, in sealed, clearly marked envelopes; an original and a copy were required. Questions were to be submitted in writing to Gregory Gatsogiannis at ggatsogiannis@shrewsburyma.gov. Respondents must provide required certifications and disclosure forms, including PERAC annual investment-consultant compliance forms, and disclose direct or indirect compensation, commissions, brokerage arrangements, benefits, employment or contractual relationships, and potential conflicts of interest. Proposals should describe qualifications, services, objectives, terms, and compensation, and demonstrate objective, unbiased advice. The Board may request additional information, interview respondents, or reject proposals. Any resulting contract is subject to applicable Massachusetts law and PERAC regulations; it may include extensions and may be terminated with 30 days’ notice.

result.title: Page 3
result.summary: The document is a request for proposals from investment consultants serving the Shrewsbury Retirement Board. It asks firms to describe their history, ownership and organizational structure; services, clients, investment activities, affiliates, subsidiaries and business relationships; offices, staffing, qualifications, experience, roles, workload and employee departures; and their ethics, culture and methods for maintaining objectivity and fiduciary duty. Respondents must disclose conflicts of interest, litigation, complaints, fraud or criminal allegations, regulatory actions, claims, errors or omissions, and relevant insurance or bonding, and provide information on SEC registration, brokerage or account arrangements, and investment products and services. Submission instructions cover the required written proposal, sealed-envelope delivery and deadline, contact and identification details, and rules for modifying or withdrawing a bid; the Board reserves the right to reject proposals.

result.title: Page 4
result.summary: The text is a request for information about the Company’s investment services, asset-allocation and investment-management processes, fees, and client experience. It asks about investment philosophy and policy development; portfolio objectives, asset/liability modeling, asset classes, manager selection and oversight, performance measurement, rebalancing, underperformance and manager replacement or termination; and reporting, tools, data, customization, custody, trading, transition, and service delivery. It also seeks fee and compensation details, revenue sources, commissions, broker arrangements and soft-dollar practices, along with conflict safeguards and administrative policies. The Company is asked to explain its fiduciary role, services and competitive distinctions, and provide its U.S. experience, including Massachusetts clients. Finally, it requests current and former client references from the past five years—preferably pension plans—with contact details, plan type and size, services and service duration, plus information on terminated clients and service continuity.

result.title: Page 5
result.summary: The text outlines requirements for evaluating and selecting an investment consultant for a Massachusetts retirement system. It asks the Board to describe its RFP procedures, proposal opening and evaluation process, criteria and weighting, ranking, treatment of nonresponsive bids and minor errors, and how the most advantageous proposal will be identified. Evaluation may consider qualifications, services, investment expertise and performance, fiduciary ability, objectives, and cost. Proposers should disclose compensation, fees, commissions, brokerage and other direct or indirect benefits, including payments involving affiliates, investment managers, clients, or asset placement, and explain related arrangements. The text also addresses conflicts of interest, client relationships, indemnification, use of databases or proxy-voting services, and assistance with selecting or monitoring investment managers. It references compliance with applicable laws and Massachusetts General Laws, Chapter 32, §23B(k)(1).

result.title: Page 6
result.summary: The text sets out proposal evaluation ratings: “Unacceptable” for material failure to meet requirements, “Advantageous” for meeting them, and “Highly Advantageous” for exceeding them; optional or inapplicable items may be treated accordingly. Proposals must be concise, responsive, complete, and follow the requested format. Evaluation covers the scope and quality of services; firm and team experience with public pension funds and agencies; knowledge of Massachusetts Chapter 32, PERAC requirements, and related regulations; investment philosophy, strategy, asset allocation, and manager selection; compliance systems and regulatory updates; research, data, and reporting; and the firm’s stability, commitment, availability, and client-service record. Services include regular Board meetings, investment monitoring, performance and compliance reviews, and clear, timely reports and updates. Proposals must address all required statutory, regulatory, and investment objectives and explain how the firm and its personnel will deliver the services.

result.title: Page 7
result.summary: The text sets out bid requirements for investment-management services for the Shrewsbury Retirement Board. Bidders must provide qualifications, pricing, required forms and certifications (including non-collusion and tax information), and documentation demonstrating their ability to perform and comply with applicable laws, regulations, and pension-system requirements. The Board may request further information, conduct investigations or interviews, and assess firms’ investment methods, financial information, reporting, fees, and proposed services. The successful firm may be required to support Board and committee reviews, recommendations, reports, and investment-related work. The Board may determine bidder qualifications and accept or reject any or all bids, with award decisions made in its judgment and best interests. The awarded bidder must complete and sign the contract within the specified period, generally 45 days after award or notification, unless the Board sets an earlier deadline. The text also addresses tax treatment and possible tax exemption.

result.title: Page 8
result.summary: The text sets out bid and contract requirements for the Town of Shrewsbury. Bids must be properly signed: individuals sign in ink, partnerships provide the required partners’ signatures, and corporations use the corporate name and seal with an authorized signature. The bidder must certify compliance with Massachusetts conflict-of-interest laws, including Chapter 268A, and that no prohibited public official or employee has an interest in the agreement. The successful bidder must indemnify, defend, and hold the Town harmless from claims, injury, or property damage arising from the work, and take precautions to prevent them. The Town may cancel a bid or agreement in cases of improper conduct or noncompliance; award and performance are subject to the stated contract terms.
